LESSON: SKIMMING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading 2.5 Reading Aloud (Articulation) (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub- stra
Topic 2.6: Skimming for information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Skimming for information, part of Reading 2.5 Reading Aloud (Articulation) (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub- stra in Grade 9 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: When do you read a text for specific information?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read out loud a list of various meals one can order from their local restaurant,

2. listen to and read along to an audio/video about restaurant situations,

3. read texts from peers about ordering food in restaurants (z.B. Ich möchte bitte___; Darf ich ____ bestellen/haben?; Danke; Bitte schön, usw),

4. read and role-play ordering food in a restaurant,

5. listen to and read along texts about ordering for food/drinks using specific quantities (z.B. Ich ,möchte eine TasseTee, bitte; Darf ich bitte eine Tasse Tee?; Ich möchte eine Flasche Wasser, bitte, usw),

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read out loud a list of various meals one can order from their local restaurant,
2. listen to and read along to an audio/video about restaurant situations,
3. read texts from peers about ordering food in restaurants (z.B. Ich möchte bitte___; Darf ich ____ bestellen/haben?; Danke; Bitte schön, usw),
4. read and role-play ordering food in a restaurant,
5. listen to and read along texts about ordering for food/drinks using specific quantities (z.B. Ich ,möchte eine TasseTee, bitte; Darf ich bitte eine Tasse Tee?; Ich möchte eine Flasche Wasser, bitte, usw),

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Skimming for information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital Literacy: the learner develops the skills of interacting with digital technology when s/he searches online for menus

from Germany and shares with peers.

Values:
Responsibility: the learner develops awareness for excellence in proactively solving problems as s/he searches online for

menus from Germany and shares the knowledge with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health Education - healthy eating habits: the learner develops an awareness of healthy eating habits when s/he reads out loud a

list of various meals one can order from their local restaurant.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner links acquired communication skills when they practise ordering food to the same learnt in English and Kiswahili.

The vocabulary of foodstuff learnt links to the same concept in Agriculture.
